name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Salinas is an incumbent in a D+6 district
No expert raters or polls flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Salinas: a D+6 seat, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial advantage against a challenger who has raised almost nothing. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays close to the baseline with a slight trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending showing Russ gaining traction would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Andrea Salinas seeks a second term in Oregon's 6th District, a seat Democrats hold with a six-point partisan lean. She has raised about $1.6 million and holds over $600,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has raised roughly $13,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against her, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets put her chances around 96 percent. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the stark money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic win in this Portland-area swing-trending seat.
